subject: Pinnacle AI — Networking sprint charter & private link sequencing
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@pinnacle.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pinnacle.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Private deployment networking and turn-up sequencing

Hi Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have internal approval to move forward with a private deployment. Before we kick off procurement I need to align our network and security teams on expected cadence and what Redwood will require for VPC peering vs private endpoints.

High level asks from our side:
- A recommended VPC CIDR layout and whether Redwood prefers peering or PrivateLink for initial MVP.
- A list of artifacts we should provide to your infra team (routing table, firewall rules, sample service account).
- Rough sprint cadence: is a two-week network sprint reasonable prior to on-prem appliance shipping?

Can you point us to a short checklist or a sprint charter we can use to coordinate with our cloud team? We want to get a procurement hold on hold until the networking work is scoped.

Best,
Aaron Lee
Head of Infrastructure
Pinnacle AI
aaron.lee@pinnacle.ai

---
Attachment: pinnacle_network_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@pinnacle.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking and turn-up sequencing

Aaron —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answer: we can support both options but prefer VPC peering for the first wave when customers want lower setup complexity, and PrivateLink/Private Endpoint for tighter isolation in the next phase. I'll outline a proposed sprint charter below and loop in the implementation leads.

Pre-sprint deliverables from Pinnacle:
- Primary VPC CIDR list (a /16 or /20 preference?)
- Public IPs for NAT/GW (if any) and egress policy
- Service account email for Redwood to grant temporary certs

Proposed network sprint (2 weeks):
Week 0 (Prep): Exchange CIDRs, share diagram (you already attached a great start).
Week 1: VPC peering config, test routing and latency checks, initial private endpoints (if chosen) in test subnet.
Week 2: Validation, PKI cert exchange, security review, and smoke test of inference traffic.

I'll have Monica run the tech ops cadence and Grace take point for security/compliance checks. Aditya will be on-call for kernel/runtime tuning once traffic starts.

Can you confirm internal attendees for a 60-minute kickoff Thursday (your timezone)? If so, I'll send a calendar invite and an initial sprint charter doc.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood_private_deploy_checklist_v2.xlsx (checklist, 220KB)

From: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pinnacle.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@pinnacle.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 May 2028 13:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking and turn-up sequencing

Marcus —

Thursday works for us. Attendees: myself (cloud infra lead), Aaron (Head of Infra), Diego (network eng, will forward separate), and security: Priya N. (cc'd on separate thread). We prefer to start with VPC peering and then evaluate a PrivateLink cutover in sprint 2.

One quick question: do you require a dedicated edge appliance for the on-prem package, or is an initial cloud-only path acceptable for our first MVP? That will determine procurement timing.

Thanks,
Sara Gomez
Cloud Infrastructure Manager
Pinnacle AI

---
Note: Diego and Priya will be added to the kickoff; they are external to Redwood.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pinnacle.ai>, Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@pinnacle.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking and turn-up sequencing

Sara/Aaron —

Thanks — confirming Thu 2028-05-05 16:00 UTC as kickoff (I've sent calendar invite). To answer Sara's question: for the MVP we can run cloud-only (Redwood-hosted control plane + VPC peering) and ship an on-prem appliance in parallel if you plan to host inference locally. If you want the appliance, procurement lead time is 4–6 weeks.

For the kickoff I'll attach a short sprint charter (outline) and a CIDR worksheet. Action items for kickoff:
- Pinnacle: confirm target VPC CIDRs and list of test subnets (A/B).
- Pinnacle: provide a point of contact for cert exchange and an initial passwordless-service-account email.
- Redwood: supply peer request template and suggested routing policy.

We'll run day-to-day on an internal sprint channel (we'll create a shared Slack) and use the Drive folder Aaron linked.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

---
Attachment: pinnacle_vpc_cidr_sheet.csv (CSV, 2KB)

From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@pinnacle.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@pinnacle.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 May 2028 10:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment networking and turn-up sequencing

Monica/Marcus —

Thanks for the clarity. We've decided to proceed with cloud-first (VPC peering) for the MVP and request the appliance for sprint 2. Attached is the CIDR sheet and a short network contact list. We'll confirm cert contact (security) on Monday.

A couple of clarifications for the sprint charter:
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 120ms from our east-us subnets to your inference endpoints. Is that achievable with peering?
- Can Redwood provide a sample iptables/egress rule set we should adapt?

I'll be on the kickoff and will have Diego on the call for routing specifics.

Aaron

Date: Mon, 07 May 2028 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Sprint charter accepted — next steps and pre-kickoff checklist

Aaron/Sara —

Following the kickoff and the spreadsheet review, this is the agreed sprint charter and pre-kickoff checklist (final):

Sprint cadence: 10 business days
Objectives:
- Establish VPC peering, route propagation, and basic egress rules
- Exchange certs and validate TLS handshake for inference traffic
- Run synthetic workload and confirm p95 < 120ms (target)

Pre-kickoff checklist (Pinnacle items):
1) Finalize CIDRs in the shared CSV (done).
2) Provide test subnet IDs and QoS tagging guidance (by 2028-05-09).
3) Temporary service account email for cert provisioning (by 2028-05-09).

Redwood items:
1) Peer request template (shared in Drive).
2) iptables/egress guidance (sample included).
3) Test harness for synthetic traffic (we'll provide a container image).

Risks & mitigations:
- If procurement delays appliance shipping, we proceed cloud-first and schedule appliance cutover for sprint 2.
- If latency exceeds SLO in staging, Redwood will provide a hardware tuning pass and investigate edge placement to reduce hop count.

I've uploaded the final sprint charter to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aPinnacleOnboard

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
